system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:23 UTC, the proxy recorded a successful HTTPS CONNECT tunnel from WS-BCARTER-01 to drive.google.com, with a Chrome user agent.

Several later connections from WS-BCARTER-01 went to the internal proxy at 10.30.20.30:8080; some transferred substantial response volumes, but these records do not identify the external destinations.
At 13:46 UTC, DC-HD-01 recorded Kerberos ticket activity for ben.carter from 10.30.10.24, targeting WS-BCARTER-01$; the available records do not identify the source host.
DropboxUpdate.exe ran briefly as SYSTEM on WS-BCARTER-01 at about 14:11–14:12 UTC. This establishes updater execution, not Dropbox file-sync activity.

The Google Drive tunnel and the unidentified proxied traffic merit investigation because the inventory does not approve other file-sharing or cloud-storage services; the evidence does not establish that data was uploaded or that the activity was malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The sampled Zeek records identify connections from WS-BCARTER-01 to the internal proxy, but do not reveal the external destinations or originating processes for those flows (T006-00123, T006-00204, T006-00319).
The available proxy CONNECT records provide destination and user-agent details for specific connections, not for the later proxied flows in the alert period (T006-00016, T006-00348, T006-00350).
The Kerberos records identify 10.30.10.24 as the source of ticket activity but do not map that IP to a host or show the outcome of a logon to WS-BCARTER-01 (T006-00190, T006-00191).
claims_not_established: Whether the periodic HTTPS activity was malicious, benign, or related to the Google Drive tunnel.
Whether data was uploaded, downloaded, or otherwise transferred to an external service.
Which external destinations and processes generated the unidentified proxied connections.
Which host used 10.30.10.24 and whether its Kerberos activity was authorized.
Whether Dropbox synchronization or file transfer occurred; the records show only the updater process.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy logs for the full review window, including destination hostnames, authenticated user, request details, byte counts, and correlation to client connections.
Endpoint process and network telemetry around the periodic connections, including process-to-connection attribution and relevant browser or application activity.
Asset and DHCP/IP assignment records for 10.30.10.24, plus corresponding authentication and logon records.
Endpoint evidence establishing whether a Dropbox client or other file-sync software was installed or active, and whether files were transferred.
